provenance: Original fictional teaching material authored for this library. Expected values are human-defined answer keys, not actual AI run results.

cases.title: Find an approved review interval and owner without inventing a budget

documents.title: Pilot knowledge-library review policy
documents.text: Approved policy for the fictional Aster pilot knowledge library. Review every knowledge-library entry every 30 days. Mira is the policy owner and maintains the review register. This policy does not specify a budget.

documents.title: Office lunch notes
documents.text: The cafeteria serves soup on Tuesdays. The office reading club meets near the window. These notes are unrelated to knowledge-library governance.

questions.question: How many days are between required knowledge-library reviews?
Who owns the approved review policy?
What is the approved annual budget in USD?

review_checks: The answer cites the policy's docid for both supported claims, not the unrelated lunch notes.
The unknown budget remains null; inspected document IDs explain the evidence boundary without pretending to support a number.
Human review confirms the actual cited passage and approval status. This text fixture does not check OCR or retrieval.

cases.title: Separate a commitment from a suggestion

inputs.speaker_names: Names below are defined by this fictional transcript, not inferred from diarization labels.

segments.speaker: Mira
segments.text: I will send the revised onboarding checklist by 2026-10-21.

segments.speaker: Jun
segments.text: I will validate the export sample by 2026-10-22.

segments.speaker: Leo
segments.text: Maybe we could build a dashboard. I am only suggesting it; we have not agreed an owner or a date.

segments.speaker: Mira
segments.text: Keep the dashboard as a proposal for discussion. There is no commitment to build it yet.

review_checks: Exactly two commitments exist; speaker proximity does not turn Leo into a dashboard owner.
The proposal's owner and due_date stay null rather than being copied from another row or the meeting date.
Paraphrases may differ while preserving meaning. This fixture does not test audio recognition or real identity matching.
No extracted item authorizes sending a message or creating a task.

cases.title: Preserve an unknown price and row provenance

inputs.source_mode: provided fictional page text only; do not navigate to the .invalid URLs

pages.content: Lumen Desk — a fictional shared planning tool. The Solo plan costs USD 12 per month, billed monthly. Includes one workspace.
Harbor Board — a fictional team checklist tool. Includes shared checklists and a read-only overview. Contact the team to discuss plans. No price is listed on this page.

review_checks: There is one row per supplied page, with its exact source URL and source_id.
Unstated price is null, not zero, free, a quote from another product, or an inferred yearly conversion.
These are fictional page texts; passing this case does not establish real website navigation compatibility.

cases.title: Calculate a weighted completion rate before narrating it

inputs.grain: one row per team and week; planned and done are item counts

calculation_rules.change_percentage_points: current unrounded rate minus previous unrounded rate

review_checks: All four rows are counted once, and each team-week combination is unique.
Rates are computed from summed counts rather than an unweighted average of team rates.
Use a numeric tolerance of 0.005 for displayed two-decimal metrics; label the difference as percentage points, not relative percent.
The rows do not explain why the rate changed or establish an AI productivity benefit.

cases.title: A newer proposal does not replace an approved rule

inputs.question: What acknowledgment time currently applies to the fictional Aster pilot support queue, and what change is proposed?

sources.title: Approved Aster support acknowledgment rule
sources.text: Approved rule: the Aster pilot support queue must acknowledge each new request within 2 hours. This rule remains effective until an approved replacement takes effect.

sources.title: Draft change for review
sources.text: Proposal only, not approved: change the acknowledgment window from 2 hours to 3 hours. Approval and an effective date are pending. This draft does not change the current rule.

review_checks: Current and proposed hours are distinct; recency is not treated as approval.
Each factual conclusion cites the source that actually supports it.
The reviewer checks publication date, effective date, and approval status individually.
This supplied-source exercise cannot establish whether other live sources exist.

cases.title: Keep a six-slide pilot update inside its evidence

facts.text: The fictional Aster pilot ran for 4 weeks.
The participating teams were Docs and Ops.
The pilot explored document question answering and weekly reporting.
The next-phase decision is pending. No rollout has been approved.
Document question answering and weekly reporting were explored.
The next-phase decision is pending; no rollout is approved.

review_checks: Alternative outlines are allowed when they use at most six slides and cover all six facts with valid source IDs.
Check 4 weeks, 18 people, and 12 interviews exactly; do not infer a response rate or savings percentage.
Every factual statement on actual slides points to its source; a source label alone does not prove that the claim is faithful.
Inspect the exported deck for legibility, clipping, and editability. JSON outline checks cannot establish those properties.
No new outcome, quote, or approved rollout is invented.
